title: Can a shallow-alignment depth audit identify which fine-tuning datasets caused shallowness?

original_idea.problem: Which specific data properties drive shallowness in alignment has not been ablated.
original_idea.direction: Fine-tune a base model on synthetic safety datasets with controlled first-token distributions. Measure alignment depth after each training variant.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Directly identifies the data-level fix for shallow alignment. Can inform safety data curation practices.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: first-token concentration in training data -> shallow alignment -> identifying data-level fix -> actionable improvement to safety training. Every link is explicit and leads to a concrete safety improvement.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires fine-tuning a base model multiple times with controlled synthetic datasets, measuring KL curves, and running attack evaluations. This is advanced for beginner CS students in 30 hours, even with medium compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Deliverable requires sustained effort: generating synthetic datasets with controlled properties, running 3+ training variants, measuring depth after each. Multiple experimental dimensions before reaching first result.

novelty.reasoning: Qi et al. (2024) 'Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just a Few Tokens Deep' (ICLR 2025) established that shallow alignment is driven by first-token distribution shortcuts. The March 2026 paper 'Why Is RLHF Alignment Shallow? A Gradient Analysis' (arXiv:2603.04851) formally proves that gradient-based alignment concentrates on early positions due to the harm horizon, explaining why shallowness arises. 'Few Tokens, Big Leverage' (arXiv:2603.07445, 2026) proposes constraining safety tokens during fine-tuning. However, none of these perform controlled ablations on synthetic dataset properties (e.g., first-token distributions) to isolate which data characteristics cause shallowness. The specific experimental design of varying synthetic safety datasets with controlled properties is partially novel, but the conceptual understanding is well-established.
